guideline: Five nearly native English speakers rated each example based on domain relevance, label preservation, linguistic acceptability (1-5 scale), and word error rate
- Raters evaluated generated examples based on domain relevance, label preservation, linguistic acceptability, and word error rate.
Raters were asked to assess domain relevance, label preservation, linguistic acceptability, and word error rate for each generated example.

five nearly native English speakers rated each example, considering the following evaluation measures: (1) Domain relevance (D.REL) -whether the topic of the generated text is related to its destination domain; (2) Label preservation (L.PRES)what is the label of the generated example (and we report whether the answer was identical to the desired label); (3) Linguistic Acceptability (ACCPT)how logical and grammatical the example is (on a 1-5 scale); and (4) Word error rate (WER)

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. Main issues were redundant entries and inconsistent formatting. The paper focuses on domain counterfactual generation as an NLG task and uses both automatic metrics (WER) and human evaluation. No LLM-based evaluation is used.
